subject: Business Models
title: Platform Labor Rights
description: A short lesson to help you apply Platform Labor Rights.

hook.text: Uber drivers earn an average of $15/hour before expenses. They have no health insurance or paid leave.

buildup.text: Platforms classify workers as independent contractors, not employees. This avoids taxes and benefits obligations.

discovery.text: California's AB5 law tried to reclassify gig workers as employees. Uber spent $200 million fighting it.

twist.text: The UK Supreme Court ruled Uber drivers are workers, not contractors. The law varies wildly by country.

climax.text: Platform labor debates will reshape the gig economy. The contractor model may not survive regulation.

punchline.text: Flexible work or labor exploitation? The law hasn't decided yet.

quiz.question: How do platforms typically classify their workers?

details.summary: Platform labor rights address the employment status and protections of workers who provide services through platforms like Uber, DoorDash, and TaskRabbit. The debate centers on whether gig workers are independent contractors or employees deserving minimum wage and benefits.
details.whyItMatters: Millions of workers depend on platform income without traditional employment protections. Legal rulings and legislation worldwide are redefining the relationship between platforms and their workforce.
takeaways: Gig workers' employment classification remains contested globally
Independent contractor status saves platforms employee benefit costs
Courts and legislatures are increasingly granting gig workers more protections

faq.question: Why does the independent contractor vs employee distinction matter?
faq.answer: Employees receive minimum wage guarantees, overtime pay, health insurance contributions, unemployment benefits, and workers' compensation. Independent contractors receive none of these. Reclassification would increase platform costs by 20-30% and fundamentally change their economics.

faq.question: How are different countries approaching platform worker classification?
faq.answer: The UK Supreme Court ruled Uber drivers are workers with minimum rights. California's AB5 classified gig workers as employees before Prop 22 created exceptions. The EU proposed a directive presuming platform workers are employees. Approaches vary widely by jurisdiction.
